user.title: ClimateML
user.description: Add the ClimateML integration. Add zones and configure the controller via the integration page after setup.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Only one ClimateML instance is allowed

data_description.name: Display name — also generates the stable internal zone ID
data_description.head_entity: The climate entity for this zone — ClimateML will command its setpoint to cool the space
data_description.sensor_entity: Actual room temperature sensor — reference used to determine whether cooling is needed
data_description.default_setpoint_c: Cooling setpoint used when no schedule block is active (10–32°C)
data_description.default_mode: eco applies a 1°C deadband above the setpoint; comfort triggers immediately at the setpoint
data_description.is_starvation_priority: Enable starvation logic for this zone — when enabled, other zones are suppressed if this zone cannot achieve deep cooling for 30 minutes
data_description.eva_in_entity: Refrigerant temperature entering the indoor unit — logged for ML efficiency analysis
data_description.eva_out_entity: Refrigerant temperature leaving the indoor unit — logged for ML efficiency analysis
data_description.demand_delta_entity: Setpoint minus actual head temperature — measures how much cooling the head is demanding
data_description.head_thermal_delta_entity: EVA inlet minus room temperature — measures how effectively the head is cooling
data_description.occupancy_entity: Presence sensor — when occupied in eco mode, automatically upgrades to comfort for that tick
data_description.humidity_entity: Humidity sensor — logged for future ML comfort modelling
data_description.door_entity: Door open/close sensor — logged to detect thermal leakage events
data_description.window_entity: Window open/close sensor — logged to detect thermal leakage events
data_description.blocks: Schedule blocks — each block sets a cooling setpoint and mode for a time range on weekdays or weekends

data_description.update_interval_minutes: How often ClimateML recalculates and commands each zone — lower is more responsive, higher sends fewer commands
data_description.setpoint_min_c: Lowest temperature ClimateML will ever command to any zone climate entity
data_description.setpoint_max_c: Highest temperature ClimateML will ever command to any zone climate entity
data_description.vacation_setpoint_c: Setpoint applied to all zones when Vacation Mode is on — typically a warm permissive temperature (18–28°C)
data_description.idle_head_threshold_minutes: If the room is warming but won't reach the trigger threshold for this many minutes, the head turns off to save energy (15–180 min)
data_description.eco_tolerance_c: Extra deadband added above the setpoint in eco mode before cooling triggers — prevents unnecessary compressor starts (0.0–2.0°C)
data_description.odu_mode_entity: Current operating mode of the outdoor unit — logged to correlate system state with zone decisions
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Outside air temperature — used as a peer reading in the sensor guard anomaly check
data_description.extra_temp_entities: Non-zone indoor sensors (hallway, landing, etc.) — used as peer readings in the sensor guard
data_description.power_entity: Real-time system power draw — logged for future efficiency and COP tracking
data_description.energy_entity: Cumulative system energy use — source for the Energy Today sensor and daily efficiency trends
data_description.weather_entity: Provides hourly forecasts for anticipating solar gain and outdoor conditions (future ML)
